UPSTREAM: cbmem: rename vdat to chromeos_acpi There is a confusingly named section in cbmem called vdat. This section holds a data structure called chromeos_acpi_t, which exposes some system information to the Chrome OS userland utility crossystem. Within the chromeos_acpi_t structure, there is a member called vdat. This (currently) holds a VbSharedDataHeader. Rename the outer vdat to chromeos_acpi to make its purpose clear, and prevent the bizarreness of being able to access vdat->vdat. Additionally, disallow external references to the chromeos_acpi data structure in gnvs.c. UPSTREAM: ifdtool: port the feature to set AltMeDisable/HAP bit here Port the newest feature of me_cleaner to ifdtool (https://github.com/corna/me_cleaner/ , Discussed in https://github.com/corna/me_cleaner/issues/53 ) to set AltMeDisable (or HAP for skylake/ME11) bit to the IFD to disable ME. [autotest] network_WiFi_BgscanBackoff: stop using Whirlwind's phy2 The 5760noise_check variant of this test was requesting 1 spatial stream, so that it could run on Whirlwind's phy2. Don't do this, because phy2 is not normally used in production as a transmitter, and because our lab conductive setups don't usually wire up its antennas. As an effect of this, we can't support 2 simultaneous channels on the 5 GHz band. Just use different channels from the 2.4 and 5 GHz bands. Per Kirtika's suggestion, I make the 5760noise_check variant roughly comparable to the wifi_bgscan_backoff variant, so that we can see whether channel 153 (a known noisy channel) behaves significantly differently than a known less-noisy 5GHz channel. BUG=chromium:774808, chromium:866181 TEST=network_WiFi_BgscanBackoff.wifi_bgscan_backoff and network_WiFi_BgscanBackoff.5760_noise_check with gale; both now pass; run w/ whirlwind, and see we avoid phy2 Change-Id: I22227cee072d362ceb00bda39876717a374a1d44 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1162983 Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org>

arc: Set a proper security.restorecon_last value on P Since P's image has different file_contexts than N, we need to update the logic. Without this, even eve-arcnext (the fastest) takes 1-2 seconds to restore /data's context on every boot: <6>init: Command 'restorecon --recursive --skip-ce /data' action=post-fs-data (/init.rc:547) took 1353ms and succeeded With this, it's instant except for the initial boot after OTA: <6>selinux: SELinux: Skipping restorecon_recursive(/data) Since the new logic is too complicated to write in sh, this CL moves it to arc-setup. This does not change N's behavior at all. BUG=b:112101875 TEST=boot ARC++ full container twice, check /var/log/arc.log TEST=No errors from arc-setfattr.conf in arc.log TEST=On N, 'getfattr -n security.restorecon_last /opt/../data/' (and /cache) returns the same value as before. Testlog: Remove flush mode and add a new method FlushEvent The flush mode in Testlog is designed to flush a new test_run event when any wrapped Testlog method is called. However, this may have performance issue and create too many useless events. Instead of creating an event per call, we call FlushEvent to create an event when needed.
